## PM grading, ruling + dispatch order — R20

Graded and claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6143-components-schema-import`.

### Ruling: **option 2 — measured first**

Make the blocks **import instead of re-declare**. Option 1 is #4653's approach at scale and the card's own evidence convicts it: #4653 was this exact defect, found by eye, closed one page at a time, and it came back — an approach with no guard buys one clean sweep and no floor.

**Option 3 is rejected for the reason this seat has now applied three times** (#6122 option B, #6138 option 4, here): ⛔ *a checker whose job is to keep a second source of truth honest is machinery so a divergent copy can safely persist.* Option 2 **deletes** the second source of truth; option 3 institutionalises it and then hires a guard. And option 3 has to answer "what may a page legitimately omit" — a question option 2 never has to ask, because a subset of an imported type is just a subset.

⭐ **This is the same ruling, on the same class, as #6138 one lane over** — the `content/docs/fields` pages whose `Field Schema` blocks declare their own interface and compile vacuously. Same disease, same medicine, and #6138 round 2 is in flight implementing it right now. ⚠️ **Read #6138's thread before you design anything here** — its round-1 measurement and my ruling on it are the precedent, and two lanes solving one problem two different ways is its own defect. Where you can share a shape with it, share it.

### ⛔ But measure before you fix — the card is right that the denominator is unknown

Only **5 of roughly 80** `content/docs/components` pages were swept, and 4 divergences fell out of those 5. ⛔ Do not extrapolate that rate and do not start editing on it. **Step 1 is the full sweep**: every `content/docs/components` page, documented props compared against the shipped interface body **plus everything inherited from `BaseSchema`** (so `className`, `disabled` and friends are correctly counted as real, exactly as the 5-page sweep did).

Report that number before implementing. Two things it decides:

1. Whether this lands as one PR or several, and how they batch.
2. ⚠️ Whether any page's divergence is **not** a doc error. A documented key the renderer genuinely reads but the type does not declare is an **undeclared-but-consumed capability** — a types defect, not a docs defect, and it goes to a separate card rather than being edited away. The 5-page sweep checked the renderer for all four divergences and found none consumed; keep doing that, because it is the check that stops this card silently deleting a real feature.

⛔ **STOP AND REPORT** if the sweep turns up a page shape where option 2 cannot work — a `## Schema` block describing a type that is not exported at all, for instance. That is a ruling, not an implementation detail. Round 1 of #6138 stopping on exactly this kind of finding is why the fix there is now correct instead of destructive.

### The four already measured — fix them, and note what else the type says

| page | documented | shipped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `form/radio-group.mdx` | `direction` | **`orientation`** — `form.d.ts:377` |
| `form/combobox.mdx` | `searchPlaceholder`, `emptyText` | **neither declared** |
| `form/command.mdx` | `CommandItem.shortcut` | `CommandItem` declares only `value`, `label`, `icon` |
| `feedback/toast.mdx` | `variant: 'default' \| 'destructive'` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'info'` |

⚠️ `toast.mdx` is the one to get right and the card says why: `'destructive'` is **not a member**, it is the Shadcn vocabulary a reader arrives with, and it is the value most likely to be copied. The page also **omits** four real variants plus `position` (`feedback.d.ts:133`) and `onDismiss` (`feedback.d.ts:144`). ⚠️ Omissions are not errors — a reference page may show a subset — but decide deliberately and say so, rather than leaving it to whatever the rewrite happens to carry over.

### ⛔ Standing refusals

- ⛔ **Do not mint a type, an export, or a union member** to make any documented prop true. Seventh time this session (#5329, #6107, #6122, #6126, #6135-adjacent, #6138). Documentation follows the code.
- ⛔ **No `FRAGMENT_MARKER`** — these are genuinely TypeScript. Declared fragments must come back unmoved, and that number is the proof.
- ⛔ **Do not re-fence anything.** `content/docs/components` is #5867's lane and is **blocked on #6132**. Measure through a throwaway re-fence probe under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, never committed. This card changes what the blocks *say*; #5867 changes how they are *fenced*.
- ⛔ **Do not touch #6132's five files** — `sonner`, `context-menu`, `menubar`, `dropdown-menu`, `button-group`. They are with the maintainer. PR #6142 left them byte-identical and so must this.

### Verification

- ⭐ **The vacuity is the thing being fixed, so prove it was there and is gone.** On `main`, inject a wrong key into a `## Schema` block and show the gate reports the page **green**; after your change, the same injection **reddens** it. Same page, same key, opposite verdicts. Mutation confirmed on disk by grep before any result is read. That single pair is the whole case for this card, and without it the PR is a rewrite with no evidence it bought anything.
- The full sweep's number, and the renderer check for every divergence.
- Every imported type name shown to resolve against the **shipped** `dist/*.d.ts` — build first, quote the gate's own resolution control line.
- Declared fragments unmoved; covered/ungated sets unmoved.
- Gates per your diff, each quoting its **own** verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe. vitest from the repo **root**, never package-scoped (objectui#3378).
- Render-check a sample from the prerendered HTML — this rewrite changes what the reader copies, not just whether it compiles.

⚠️ **Commit your fix before any ablation whose restore leg is `git checkout`** — a bare `git checkout --` wiped an entire uncommitted fix on this card's sibling today. Use `git checkout HEAD --` followed by the path. ⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack, other agents are using it now.

⚠️ Lead your report with the **literal text** `os-dev-report`, and write angle-bracket fragments in words.

Refs: #6138 (same class, same ruling, in flight — read it first) · #6122 / PR #6142 (where this was measured) · #5867 (the lane) · #4653 (the class, closed per-page, recurred) · #6132 (what is off-limits).

## STOPPED at step 1 as the dispatch order requires — option 2's mechanism is capped on this lane, and the cap is already a maintainer ruling

`status: needs_decision`. No PR. Branch `claude/issue-6143-components-schema-import` is pushed but holds **no commits** beyond `origin/main` (pushed empty as the write-route probe). Worktree clean.

The order's stop condition fired, in a stronger form than the example it gave:

> STOP AND REPORT if the sweep turns up a page shape where option 2 cannot work — a `## Schema` block describing a type that is not exported at all, for instance.

That shape exists (11 names). But the sweep found something that decides the card before those 11 matter: **option 2's central claim cannot be delivered for 73 of the 87 importable names**, and the reason is already filed, measured, and ruled by the maintainer as **#5155**.

---

## The blocker, proved with the gate itself

`BaseSchema` (`packages/types/dist/base.d.ts:230`) ends with an index signature that is deliberate and documented:

```
    /**
     * Additional properties specific to the component type.
     * This index signature allows type-specific extensions.
     */
    [key: string]: any;
```

An index signature disables TypeScript's excess-property check. So annotating an authored literal against `RadioGroupSchema` — option 2's exact mechanism — accepts **any** key.

### The before/after pair the order asked for, run on the real gate

I built the option-2 conversion of `form/radio-group.mdx` as a throwaway probe (re-fenced to `ts`, self-declared interface replaced by `import type` plus an annotated literal), injected the wrong key, and ran `check:doc-snippet-types`. Never committed; restored under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`; mutation confirmed on disk by grep anchored on the text I meant to change, before any result was read.

**Leg 1 — option 2 applied, wrong KEY injected (`direction`, where the shipped slot is `orientation`):**

```
  injected 'import type { RadioGroupSchema }' occurrences: 1
  injected wrong key "direction: 'vertical'," occurrences: 1
  removed 'interface RadioGroupSchema {' occurrences (expect 0): 0
```

```
Scanned 222 document(s): 178 covered (74 of them hold a ts/tsx block), 44 ungated
Covered blocks: 360 - 249 to compile, 111 declared fragment(s).
Semantic phase: 249 of 249 block(s) judged, 0 failed.

Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types.
```

`GATE_EXIT=0`. The block **entered the compile population** (248 to compile becomes 249; 73 pages holding a ts block becomes 74), it **was judged**, and it is **GREEN with the wrong key sitting in it**.

⭐ **That is the finding.** Option 2 on this lane converts an *uncompiled* vacuous block into a *compiled* vacuous block. The blocks-to-compile count goes up — which is exactly the number the PM records having over-accepted #5867's batches on — while the check buys nothing for the divergence class the card is about.

**Leg 2 — wiring self-check, same page, same shape, bad VALUE on a DECLARED member (`orientation: 'diagonal'`):**

```
  [semantic]  content/docs/components/form/radio-group.mdx:41:3  TS2322: Type '"diagonal"' is not assignable to type '"horizontal" | "vertical" | undefined'.
Semantic phase: 249 of 249 block(s) judged, 1 failed.
```

`GATE_EXIT=1`. So Leg 1's green is a **measurement, not broken wiring** — the same machinery reddens the moment the divergence is one the index signature does not wave through.

**Baseline, unmodified tree**, for the delta:

```
  resolution   Module name '@object-ui/types' was successfully resolved to '/home/user/objectui-6143/packages/types/dist/index.d.ts'
  sentinel     importing 'ThisNameIsDefinitelyNotExported' produced 1 diagnostic(s) (TS2305)
  positive     importing 'ComponentSchema' produced 0 diagnostic(s)

Scanned 222 document(s): 178 covered (73 of them hold a ts/tsx block), 44 ungated
Covered blocks: 359 - 248 to compile, 111 declared fragment(s).
Semantic phase: 248 of 248 block(s) judged, 0 failed.
```

### This is #5155, and it is already ruled

**#5155** is open, `pm:queue`: *"BaseSchema's `[key: string]: any` leaves every component schema open, so a 'declare the surface' fix can never reject a misspelled TOP-LEVEL key."* Maintainer ruling recorded 2026-08-19 (verbatim reply 「全部接受」): **option C — enforce at the zod/publish boundary, phased**, plus option D's ceiling statement immediately.

⚠️ So the maintainer has already decided that the rejection point for unknown top-level keys is **not the TypeScript layer**. Option 2 is a TypeScript-layer rejection mechanism. It is asking for the guarantee that ruling explicitly declined to put there.

This card's own PM session posted the clarification on #5155 one minute after dispatching this card, and it draws exactly the line that matters here — what a tool can **READ** is not capped, what a validator can **REJECT** is:

> | what a mirror can **REJECT** | **capped** — passthrough waves an undeclared key through |
> | what a guard can **READ** | **not capped** — solvable in the type system alone |

Option 2 is a REJECT mechanism. It is on the capped side.

## The full sweep — all 76 pages, as ordered

Resolved through the gate's own `derivePackageTypePaths()`, so it reads what the gate reads:

```
RESOLUTION CONTROL (paths derived by the gate's own derivePackageTypePaths):
  @object-ui/types -> ["/home/user/objectui-6143/packages/types/dist/index.d.ts"]
  entry files from packages/*/dist/ : 47
  entry files from packages/*/src/  : 0
```

Zero `src/` leaks — every number below is the shipped surface.

| measure | count |
|---|---|
| pages under `content/docs/components` | **76** (the card estimated ~80) |
| pages with a `## Schema` heading | 76 (one, `form/toggle.mdx`, holds no block — see findings) |
| `interface` names declared in those blocks | **98** |
| documented keys checked | **604** |
| names with **no importable shipped type** | **11** |
| names importable but **OPEN** (inherit `BaseSchema`'s index signature) | **73** |
| names importable and **SEALED** (option 2 works) | **14** |
| documented keys that are **not declared members** | **68** |
| ...on OPEN types — annotation can**not** catch | **58** |
| ...on SEALED types — annotation **would** catch | **10** |

### What option 2 would and would not buy, against the four already measured

| already-measured page | divergence kind | caught by option 2? |
|---|---|---|
| `feedback/toast.mdx` — `variant: 'destructive'` | **value** on a declared member | ✅ **yes** — `TS2322`, proved by compile |
| `form/command.mdx` — `CommandItem.shortcut` | **key** on a SEALED helper type | ✅ **yes** — `TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'shortcut' does not exist in type 'CommandItem'` |
| `form/radio-group.mdx` — `direction` | **key** on an OPEN schema | ❌ **no** — proved green above |
| `form/combobox.mdx` — `searchPlaceholder`, `emptyText` | **key** on an OPEN schema | ❌ **no** |

Exactly half. ⭐ Worth noting for the ruling: the half it **does** catch includes `toast.mdx`, which the order called *"the one to get right"* — `'destructive'` is a value on a declared member, so it reddens.

### The 11 names with no importable shipped type

`sidebar.mdx` (`SidebarItem`, `SidebarGroup`) · `span.mdx` (`SpanSchema`) · `filter-builder.mdx` (`FilterCondition`) · `toggle-group.mdx` (`ToggleGroupItem`) · `layout/page.mdx` (`PageSchema`) · `layout/semantic.mdx` (`SemanticSchema`) · `header-bar.mdx` (`Breadcrumb`) · `context-menu.mdx` (`ContextMenuItem`) · `dropdown-menu.mdx` (`DropdownMenuItem`) · `menubar.mdx` (`MenubarItem`)

Three sub-shapes, and they do not want the same answer:

1. **`ToggleGroupItem` is a reachability defect, not an absence.** It is declared *and* `export`ed at `packages/types/dist/disclosure.d.ts:113` — but `index.d.ts:60` re-exports only `AccordionItem, ToggleGroupSchema, AccordionSchema, CollapsibleSchema, DisclosureSchema` from that file, and the package `exports` map has **no `./disclosure` subpath**. So a reader cannot import it by any specifier. This is objectui#5053's lesson exactly: the name set has to come from the package's *exports*, not from a grep. Fixable by adding it to the re-export list — but that is minting reachability, so it is a ruling.
2. **`sidebar.mdx` documents an API that does not exist.** Its `SidebarSchema` documents `items` and `groups` with `SidebarItem` / `SidebarGroup` helpers; the shipped `SidebarSchema` declares `nav?: NavLink[]`, `content`, `footer`, `position`, `collapsible`. Not drift in a key or two — a different shape entirely.
3. **`SpanSchema`, `PageSchema`, `SemanticSchema`, `Breadcrumb`, `FilterCondition`** resolve to nothing (`TS2724: '"@object-ui/types"' has no exported member named 'SpanSchema'. Did you mean 'AnySchema'?`). `FilterCondition` exists only in `packages/app-shell/src/.../datasetFilterCondition.js`, never shipped.

⚠️ `ContextMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuItem` and `MenubarItem` land on three of **#6132's five off-limits files**. 11 of the 68 divergent keys land on those five pages; they were measured and left byte-identical, and nothing here proposes touching them.

### The renderer check — it caught two things this card would otherwise have destroyed

Every one of the 68 divergences was checked against its renderer, per the order. **13 keys are genuinely read**, i.e. undeclared-but-consumed capabilities — a types defect, routed out as instructed:

- ⭐ **Filed as #6150** — 13 keys across `TextSchema.content`, `CarouselSchema.opts/orientation/itemClassName`, `TreeViewSchema.nodes/onNodeClick/title`, `CheckboxSchema.required`, `FileUploadSchema.buttonText/wrapperClass`, `FilterBuilderSchema.wrapperClass`, `HoverCardSchema.align`, `ContextMenuSchema.trigger`. Two are behavioral, not cosmetic: `CheckboxSchema.required` drives the visible required marker; `TreeViewSchema.onNodeClick` is invoked as a callback.
- ⭐ **Filed as #6151** — `StackSchema.gap` / `.children` looked identical to that class and are **not**. `StackSchema extends Omit<FlexSchema, 'type'>`, and `Omit` over a type carrying an index signature **erases every named member**: `FlexSchema` resolves to 25 declared properties, `StackSchema` to **1** (`type`). The docs are right and the shipped type is wrong. Correcting `stack.mdx` to match its type — which is what this card would have done — would have deleted three correct entries.

Two further candidates were **rejected on inspection** rather than filed: `NavigationMenuItem.items` and `FilterField.value`. The renderer reads `schema.items` / `schema.value` off the top-level schema, not off the nested item type the docs declare them on, so those are docs-only keys, not consumed capabilities.

---

## Two smaller findings, recorded not actioned

- **`form/toggle.mdx` has no schema block at all** — its `## Schema` section reads, in full, `(Schema documentation temporarily disabled)`. It is 1 of the 76 and would be silently skipped by any conversion.
- **The whole lane is outside the compile population today.** 74 of 76 pages fence the block `plaintext`, one (`form/file-upload.mdx`) fences it `text`, one has no block. So `check-doc-snippet-types` reads **zero** of them right now. The vacuity the card describes is currently *potential* — it becomes actual the moment #5867 re-fences, which is what makes ruling before that lane moves the right sequencing.

---

## Why I did not implement the sealed 14 anyway

It would be defensible to convert just the 14 sealed names and bank the 10 divergences option 2 does catch. I did not, for two reasons that are the PM's to weigh rather than mine:

1. It would ship a change whose **PR body cannot honestly claim what the card claims**. The card's thesis is that importing deletes the second source of truth. Applied to 14 of 98 names it deletes 14% of it and leaves 73 open types re-declared exactly as before — and the blocks-to-compile count would rise, reading as more coverage than was bought. That is the specific misreading the order says #5867's batches already produced once.
2. The 14 sealed names are **helper item types** (`CommandItem`, `FilterField`, `FilterGroup`, `ButtonGroupButton`, `NavigationMenuItem`), not the `*Schema` types the pages are about. A page whose top-level schema is still a hand-written interface and whose item type is imported is a *third* shape, and inventing it mid-card is the improvisation round 1 of #6138 was praised for not doing.

---

## Decisions needed

See the structured block below. In short: option 2 delivers roughly half of what the card wants and cannot deliver the other half without #5155's program reaching this layer — and #5155's ruling deliberately put enforcement somewhere else.

## Housekeeping

- Nothing committed; `git status --short` empty; `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` = 0.
- All probes (`.probe6143/`, the re-fenced page) removed under traps; `radio-group.mdx` verified **byte-identical** to its pristine copy by `diff -q`.
- ⛔ No `FRAGMENT_MARKER` added, no gate weakened, no type/export/union member minted, no re-fencing committed, #6132's five files untouched.
- Measurement scripts live in the session scratchpad, not the repo.
